summitEvidence.fact: Wikipedia lists a South Ridge (class 3-4) among North Peak routes, but no page describes it or says where it ends

otherFacts.value: class 3-4

notes: No page describes this route's start. North Peak approaches in use: Skyline II/Hozomeen Ridge trail (NWHikers 2007, ~8 mi, 4400 ft to ridge camp) or Hozomeen Campground border swath; South Peak uses Hozomeen Lake TH. Own text says it heads for the South Peak saddle, which would suit Hozomeen Lake side, but that is inference. Two equally used starts, nothing ties route to one.

otherFacts.value: Fred Douglas and Paul Starr, Labor Day 1974

notes: No page describes this route's approach (the AAJ north-face and Zorro pages name no trailhead). South Peak routes generally use Hozomeen Lake trailhead at Hozomeen Campground (onehikeaweek) but nothing ties this north ridge to it; Lightning Creek and Skyline II are also used on this mountain.

identifiedBy.fact: AAJ first-ascent account (June 1988): start at Lightning Creek trailhead at Ross Lake, east past Willow Lake, then off trail

otherFacts.value: Johnson, Adams, Goodman, Petroske, 25-26 June 1988
about 6 hours to 6,200 ft saddle bivouac
III 5.6
Lightning Creek camps 16 mi from SR-20 on East Bank Trail; Ross Lake Resort water taxi serves east-bank drop-offs

notes: Identified by the route's own text and the AAJ page. NO coordinate from any page (NPS page prints none; no official candidate; Nominatim previously had only the river). Name is a boat/trail landing on the east shore of Ross Lake, not a road trailhead; place by name match or by hand. Real start for most parties is boat or the 16-mile East Bank Trail.

otherFacts.value: Dick Culbert and Alice Purdey, August 1968

notes: No page found that describes this route's approach; SummitPost and Mountaineers returned 403. Only lead is the sibling's Hozomeen Campground, unverified.

identifiedBy.fact: Zorro Face (west face) approach made on the Hozomeen Ridge Trail, which is reached from Skyline II (NWHikers 2007) and matches the route's own text naming Skyline II near km 55

otherFacts.value: Larson and Wehrly, late August 2013 (Zorro Face)
long day to bivouac, then downclimb gully and traverse
Skyline II route to Hozomeen Ridge: about 8 mi, 4,400 ft net gain, camp near 6,100 ft

notes: WEAK/inferred: Haley says approach is on the Hozomeen Ridge Trail and AAJ names no trailhead; Skyline II is the usual entry to that trail (NWHikers) and the route's own road text says so. Alternative is the Hozomeen Campground border swath. Border closed to travelers since 2020 per route text. Skyline II is in BC, ~7.8 km from peak.

Mountain Project (East Ridge, South Face, West Face only), Wikipedia, trailcatjim: no north route described. Standard access is the PCT north trailhead at Snoqualmie Pass, or Gold Creek to Joe Lake; neither tied to a north route. SummitPost and Mountaineers 403.
No page describes a north spur. Same as North Route: PCT Snoqualmie Pass and Gold Creek are the two used starts, nothing ties this route to either.

otherFacts.value: Mountain Project: PCT about 10 mi north of Snoqualmie Pass, or Gold Creek trail to Joe Lake then up to PCT

notes: No page describes a southwest slope. A 2024 trailcatjim report says they searched the south side for the guidebook route and did not find it. Two starts in use (PCT Snoqualmie Pass, Gold Creek), nothing ties this route.

trailhead.name: Necklace Valley Trailhead (East Fork Foss River)

identifiedBy.fact: Descent via North Ridge / Northeast Nose to Iron Cap Pass, 1 mi to Tank Lakes, then down to Necklace Valley and out to the East Fork Foss trailhead

otherFacts.value: north ridge, northeast nose, talus to Iron Cap Pass (5,300 ft), then Tank Lakes
mostly class 2, some class 3 on the descent

notes: Medium: the Tank Lakes side connects to Necklace Valley TH on a page (trailcatjim finished the traverse there), and route text excludes Chetwoot/West Fork Foss; but no page names a start for this exact route, and that traverse arrived from Dingford Creek. Peakbagger 403, WTA reports not opened. The placements agree within 100 m.

identifiedBy.fact: Hike starts at Adirondack Loj at Heart Lake; Van Hoevenberg then Algonquin trail, then herd path over Boundary Peak to Iroquois; also route text

otherFacts.value: 10.2 round trip
fee; lots fill early, overflow at end of Meadows Lane adds about 1 mi each way
Algonquin summit 4.3 mi, Iroquois about 5.1 mi one way; herd path about 1.1 mi from Algonquin

notes: Strong identification (route text plus page). No land-manager coordinate found: DEC page 404/redirect. Earlier passes' lakeplacid.com and myhikes.org points (44.1824,-73.9664 / 44.1831,-73.9638) are non-land-manager, not re-verified. Place by OSM name match.
